title: Miami Brickell Sales Galleries: Holograms Everywhere, but Can You See Your Unit?
seoTitle: Brickell Sales Galleries: Can You See Your Unit?
description: Brickell's new branded projects spend millions on high-tech sales galleries, yet buyers still cannot see their own unit or its view.
answer: Brickell developers spend two to three million dollars on sales galleries with holograms, laser dioramas and 360 projections. Yet buyers still cannot see their own unit: the view from the bedroom, the flow between rooms, the size of the bathroom. Galleries sell the dream, not certainty.
body:
If you have never been to Miami, go see Brickell. The neighbourhood is full of new developments, and the newest branded projects have built some of the most impressive sales galleries in the world.

## The technology race

Holograms. Laser dioramas. Interactive models. 360-degree projections. Developers are investing two to three million dollars each to outdo one another, and the experience is genuinely spectacular. You see the mock-up kitchen, you feel the lifestyle, you understand the brand behind the project, you see the floorplans.

## Then you ask one question

"Can I see my unit?"

The view from my bedroom. The flow from the living room to the kitchen. How large the secondary bathroom is. That is where the experience stops. After millions of dollars of gallery, it is still up to you to connect the dots and imagine your own home.

## Not a Miami problem

This happens everywhere, not only in Brickell. It is the biggest weakness in how presales are run today: developers spend heavily on selling the dream and very little on selling certainty.

## Data needs to sustain the dream

The dream is what brings a buyer through the door. But at some point, before they sign, they need data that confirms it. The developers who give buyers a clear view of their own unit are the ones who turn gallery visits into contracts.
takeaways: Brickell galleries spend millions on holograms and immersive tech.
Buyers still cannot see their own unit, its view or its room sizes.
Selling the dream is not enough; buyers need certainty before signing.
The problem is global, not specific to Miami.
faq: What is a sales gallery in real estate?
A showroom where a developer presents an off-plan project with models, finish samples, mock-ups and renderings before the building exists.
Why do buyers leave sales galleries without signing?
Often because they still cannot picture their specific unit, and that uncertainty is enough to delay or cancel the decision.
Is Brickell a good place to buy presale?
It is one of the most active presale markets in the US. As anywhere, compare presale prices with finished buildings nearby and check each developer's track record.
